summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-Y2 admits no external crate. academic-role-profile links academic-competency, academic-domain, academic-ingestion, serde and thiserror as product edges, and academic-competency, serde_json and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: the three workspace product edges are path packages this repository already builds, and serde and thiserror were admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond serde's and thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-role-profile is the P2-Y2 boundary: section 24.2's RoleProfile as a versioned competency bundle with importance levels, sources and user adjustments; support for the twelve named role directions and the specification's own openness beside them; the coexistence of two organisations' differing bundles; and a fork that records lineage without touching its base. It owns the identity, which is the lineage-and-version pair rather than section 24.2's folded id spelling; the adjustment layer, which is a second document bound to the exact version it was written over; the shelf, which is keyed on the pair and refuses to replace an occupied key; and the interest type, which holds a lineage and a standing and is not an argument to anything. It is a separate package from academic-competency because that crate owns what a performance is and this one owns which performances a role asks for, and the direction of the edge is what keeps a competency declarable without a bundle and a bundle entry impossible without a competency identity.

no_second_vocabulary_note: Section 7.1's node hierarchy and section 7.2's edge registry were implemented by P2-C1, and this task adds neither again. NodeType::RoleProfile and PredicateName::RelevantToRole already exist in academic-domain, so RoleProfile::node_type and RoleProfile::entry_predicate read that registry rather than declaring a second one. The version is the sharper case: RELEVANT_TO_ROLE's closed qualifier schema is exactly one key, role_profile_version, of kind PositiveInteger and required, so RoleProfileVersion is that qualifier rather than a number this crate chose, and the_version_qualifier_is_the_registry_s compares both the qualifier set and that kind in both directions. Section 24.2's importance -- CORE, COMMON, CONTEXT_DEPENDENT -- is deliberately NOT the registry's: RELEVANT_TO_ROLE carries no importance qualifier, unlike ENABLES_COMPETENCY's contribution_importance, so BundleImportance is read out of section 24.2's own YAML block in both directions and the qualifier-set comparison is what fails if a later registry grows one. Section 24.2's twelve direction names are read out of the specification's own sentence rather than transcribed, and the etc. that ends that sentence is RoleDirection::UserNamed, which is not one of the twelve. A calendar date is not restated either: RecordedOn wraps academic_ingestion::Date, whose module owns the separation of a document's own dates from the wall clock, so this crate adds no second calendar and has no constructor that takes an instant.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-competency: CompetencyId. P2-Y1 separated a competency from a concept into two types with no conversion in either direction, and a bundle entry names the first, so a bundle cannot name a concept, a label or a job title in that position. This crate adds no conversion of its own.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: NodeType and PredicateName, which are section 7.1's node hierarchy and section 7.2's edge registry. RELEVANT_TO_ROLE's one required qualifier, role_profile_version, is of kind PositiveInteger, and that descriptor is where RoleProfileVersion's shape comes from; QualifierKind is imported so the comparison is against the registry's own value rather than a spelling of it.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-ingestion: dating::Date, and nothing else from that crate. Section 24.2's validAt and a source's consultation date are valid time -- the document's own dates, not the clock -- and P2-U6's dating module already carries that separation with a Date that has no constructor taking an instant. Reusing it is what makes 'this crate cannot ask what time it is' survive the arrival of a dated field, which the_role_profile_crate_touches_no_file_and_no_socket measures with Instant, SystemTime and a bare now in its forbidden-construct pass.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-competency: Declared a second time for the trybuild reason academic-scenario gives: a compile-fail case compiles against this crate plus its dev-dependencies, and two of the nine cases name a competency identity.
dev_workspace_dependencies.serde_json: The schema round trip. Section 24.2's key set is read out of the specification's YAML block and compared against the serialized document, each of the nine wire keys is removed one at a time, a userAdjustments key is offered to the base bundle and refused, and three origin-versus-version disagreements are offered and refused.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Section 24.2's separations are types, and the nine cases under crates/role-profile/tests/compile_fail assert that each refusal is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic -- a favourite handed to fork, the standing that would mean a career was chosen, a label read as a direction, a layer bound to a lineage rather than a version, the rendered id spelling parsed back into a pair, an adjustment field on a base bundle, a setter on a version, a bare number where the positive-integer door belongs, and a shelf entry replaced in place.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-role-profile is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns section 24.2, whose whole content is that a role bundle is the user's own versioned claim rather than a fact about the labour market. A role name is not a market truth, and four separations hold that rather than a sentence: there is no function from RoleLabel to RoleDirection and none back, so Backend Engineer is never read as a direction; BundleShelf::by_label returns a LabelReading over a list and never one bundle, and carries a LabelAmbiguity naming the distinct lineages and scopes when it reached several, which is P2-R4's ClassificationConflict and P2-N5's tied roots one stage over; the shelf is keyed on the lineage-and-version pair and shelve refuses an occupied key, so one organisation's bundle cannot displace another's; and RoleInterest holds a lineage and a standing, is named by no public signature outside its own four functions, and its standing vocabulary has no arm meaning the user has chosen this career and none meaning a path failed, which is P2-N2's AutomaticLevel-has-no-Fluent shape and P2-U5's prediction-cannot-be-promoted shape. The identity is the pair rather than section 24.2's folded backend_engineer_profile_v4 spelling, because P2-R4 measured a concatenated-and-truncated key colliding two findings whose goal version alone differed and P2-A1 caught the same shape as a P1 defect; RoleProfileRef::rendered writes that spelling for a reader and has no inverse, no FromStr and no TryFrom<String>. An edit is a new version and a fork is a new lineage: RoleProfile has no public field, no setter and no &mut self method, nothing in the crate takes &mut self at all including the shelf, revise and fork both borrow their base, and an adjustment layer names the exact version it was written over so a layer over version three is not applied to version four. User adjustments are a second document: RoleProfile has no adjustment field and its wire denies unknown fields, so section 24.2's userAdjustments cannot ride in through JSON either. Its dependency set is minimal and the edges it does not have are the point: no academic-store, so nothing here reaches the canonical writer and no migration is added; no academic-worker and no academic-egress-boundary, so nothing in its closure can launch a process or stage a payload; and no HTTP, feed or fetch edge of any kind, which is what GATE-38-029 staying open looks like in the dependency graph.
network_posture: The crate opens no socket, opens no file, reads no clock, declares no foreign function, reads no environment variable, spawns no process, and runs no build script. It spells no std::fs name at all: every bundle, entry, adjustment, citation and date arrives as an argument. the_role_profile_crate_touches_no_file_and_no_socket in crates/role-profile/tests/role_scans.rs compares the whole set of its use items against a 27-entry inventory split into non-crate imports, crate:: imports and pub use re-exports, the whole set of the two-segment paths it reaches through a crate root -- one, thiserror::Error -- and the whole set of the macros it invokes -- two, format and matches -- against pinned inventories in both directions, and runs a whole-identifier pass for seventeen filesystem, clock, process and transport constructs over every file of the package, tests included, with Instant, SystemTime and a bare now among them. every_field_of_this_crate_is_in_the_inventory compares all 57 declared fields against a pinned inventory in both directions, requires each to say which of six things it holds, and refuses a u8 or a u64 in any declared type, so neither a byte buffer nor a clock reading has a name to arrive under; the_unnamed_fields_are_pinned closes the six tuple structs and the three enumerations with unnamed variants that a named-field comparison would miss. the_only_producers_of_a_bundle_are_the_three_doors compares the whole set of public functions returning a RoleProfile by value against declare, revise and fork, which is GATE-38-029 in the source: this build ships no bundle for any direction, and a shipped default bundle would be a fourth producer. Its link closure holds nothing that can open a socket beyond libc, which reaches it through academic-policy's bundled SQLite by way of academic-repository in P2-Y1's dev closure. Every bundle, adjustment, shelf and interest in its test tree is synthetic and built in process; no network call is made and no feed is read, because there is none.
advisory_path: Unchanged. Every external crate academic-role-profile links was admitted by an earlier receipt and is triaged through that receipt's advisory path. trybuild is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-scenario, academic-desktop, academic-proposal, academic-repository-classification, academic-repository-competency and academic-competency, and serde_json is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-competency. .github/dependabot.yml opens no version-update pull request.
